items.description: Analyze repository structure, available tooling, and agent capabilities
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/repo_analysis.md documenting: (a) all modules in .archivara/ and .opencode/ with purposes and entry points, (b) available tools (semantic_scholar commands: search/citations/references/recommend/graph/bibtex; concept_evolve commands: evolve/probe/reframe/walk), (c) agent roles defined in opencode.json (orchestrator, researcher, writer, reviewer, concept_worker) with tool permissions for each, (d) empty scaffolds (figures/, results/) and their intended contents. File must be at least 300 words with a directory-tree diagram.

items.description: Conduct comprehensive web-based literature review on N-body gravity simulation methods
items.acceptance_criteria: Use web search and Semantic Scholar to survey at least 4 sub-topics: (a) classical direct-summation N-body methods and Plummer/spline softening techniques, (b) hierarchical tree codes (Barnes-Hut octree/quadtree) and fast multipole methods (Greengard-Rokhlin), (c) symplectic integrators (Stormer-Verlet/leapfrog, Yoshida higher-order, Wisdom-Holman mapping) and their conservation properties, (d) modern GPU-accelerated and parallel N-body solvers (Bonsai, NBODY6++GPU). Produce results/literature_review.md with at least 1500 words, structured sections per sub-topic, and inline citations referencing entries in sources.bib. Each section must identify at least 2 key findings relevant to a minimal Python implementation.

items.description: Create and populate sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted references
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib exists at repo root with at least 10 valid BibTeX entries containing author, title, year, and journal/booktitle fields. Required entries include: Barnes & Hut 1986 (hierarchical tree code), Verlet 1967 (integration method), Greengard & Rokhlin 1987 (fast multipole method), Aarseth 2003 (gravitational N-body simulations textbook), at least 2 symplectic integrator papers (e.g., Yoshida 1990, Wisdom & Holman 1991), at least 2 modern GPU/parallel N-body papers (post-2010), and at least 2 open-source N-body codebases (e.g., REBOUND: Rein & Liu 2012, Gadget-2: Springel 2005). Validate that each entry parses as valid BibTeX by confirming @article/@inproceedings/@book tags with matching braces.

items.description: Delegate citation-graph mining to literature-graph-miner subagent for cross-domain insights
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a literature-graph-miner subagent to traverse citation graphs seeded from Barnes & Hut 1986, Verlet 1967, and Greengard & Rokhlin 1987. Produce results/citation_graph_analysis.md containing: (a) at least 5 high-impact descendant papers (>100 citations each) with one-sentence summaries, (b) at least 3 cross-domain connections (e.g., molecular dynamics, electrostatics, cosmological simulation, SPH) with the bridging paper identified, (c) identification of 2 underexplored techniques transferable to a minimal gravity sim with justification. File must reference specific Semantic Scholar paper IDs.

items.description: Define problem scope, constraints, and measurable success criteria for the minimal gravity simulation
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/problem_definition.md specifying: (a) particle count range (minimum 2 to maximum 10000), (b) dimensionality (2D primary, optional 3D extension), (c) required integrators (Euler baseline + leapfrog required), (d) force solvers to implement (direct O(N^2) + vectorized O(N^2) + Barnes-Hut O(N log N)), (e) performance target (wall-clock < 33ms per step for N <= 500 using direct solver, i.e. 30fps capable), (f) accuracy target (relative energy drift < 0.1% over 1000 leapfrog steps with dt=0.001 on a stable 2-body orbit), (g) language and dependencies (Python 3.10+, NumPy, Matplotlib, pytest), (h) visualization requirements (static scatter/trajectory plots + energy-vs-time plot + animated GIF). Document must be at least 500 words and reference at least 3 entries from sources.bib to justify choices.

items.description: Bootstrap concept-tree exploration for gravity simulation design space
items.acceptance_criteria: Use concept_evolve 'evolve' command on the topic 'minimal N-body gravity simulation design space'. Verify that results/concept_evolve/tree/ contains at least 3 concept branches covering: (a) integration algorithms, (b) force calculation strategies, (c) spatial data structures. Each branch must have at least 2 leaf folders with concept.json and README.md files. The tree index at results/concept_evolve/tree/index.json must list all generated concept folders with their viability scores.

items.description: Implement direct-summation O(N^2) gravity solver with Plummer softening as the baseline
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/gravity/direct.py implementing: (a) Newtonian gravitational force calculation F = -G*m1*m2*(r_ij)/|r_ij|^3 with Plummer softening parameter epsilon (default 0.01), (b) function compute_accelerations(positions, masses, softening) -> accelerations as NumPy arrays, (c) brute-force O(N^2) pairwise force accumulation using explicit Python loops. Create tests/test_direct.py with pytest tests verifying: (i) two-body force magnitude matches analytical 1/r^2 law within 1% for separation >> epsilon, (ii) force symmetry (F_ij = -F_ji to machine precision) for 10 random particles, (iii) zero self-force (diagonal terms). All 3 tests must pass via 'pytest tests/test_direct.py'.

items.description: Implement Leapfrog (kick-drift-kick) and Forward Euler time integrators
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/integrators/leapfrog.py implementing kick-drift-kick leapfrog with signature step(positions, velocities, masses, dt, force_fn) -> (new_positions, new_velocities). Create src/integrators/euler.py implementing forward Euler with the same signature. Create tests/test_integrators.py verifying: (a) leapfrog relative energy drift < 0.1% over 10000 steps for a circular 2-body orbit with dt=0.001, (b) Euler energy diverges by > 5% under the same conditions (demonstrating its unsuitability), (c) leapfrog is time-reversible: run forward N steps then backward N steps, final position error < 1e-10. All tests pass via pytest.

items.description: Build metrics and benchmarking framework for timing, energy, and angular momentum tracking
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/metrics.py providing: (a) compute_total_energy(positions, velocities, masses, softening) returning kinetic + gravitational potential energy as a float, (b) compute_angular_momentum(positions, velocities, masses) returning L_z scalar for 2D, (c) TimingContext context-manager class recording wall-clock time, (d) benchmark_sweep(solver_fn, integrator_fn, n_values, n_steps) that runs simulations and records results. Output benchmark results to results/baseline_benchmarks.json with schema per entry: {solver, integrator, N, steps, wall_time_seconds, initial_energy, final_energy, energy_error_pct}. Validate by running a sweep with N in {10, 50, 100} using direct solver + leapfrog; the JSON file must contain at least 3 entries.

items.description: Create 2D visualization module for orbit plots, energy tracking, and animation
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/visualization.py with: (a) plot_snapshot(positions, masses, filename) saving a 2D scatter plot with mass-proportional marker sizes, (b) plot_trajectories(trajectory_history, filename) saving particle paths as colored lines, (c) plot_energy(time_array, energy_array, filename) saving energy-vs-time line plot, (d) create_animation(trajectory_history, filename, fps=30) saving an animated GIF using Matplotlib FuncAnimation. Generate figures/baseline_two_body.png (stable circular orbit snapshot) and figures/baseline_energy.png (energy conservation plot over 1000 steps). Both must exist as valid image files > 1KB.

items.description: Delegate subagent exploration of baseline O(N^2) bottlenecks and optimization opportunities
items.acceptance_criteria: Run baseline benchmarks for N in {10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000} using the direct solver + leapfrog integrator (appending to results/baseline_benchmarks.json). Then launch a concept-tree-explorer subagent to analyze the timing data. Produce results/concept_evolve/tree/bottleneck_analysis/analysis.md identifying: (a) the dominant computational bottleneck with quantified wall-time fraction, (b) the N threshold where wall-time exceeds 33ms per step (real-time breakpoint), (c) at least 3 optimization strategies ranked by expected speedup, referencing prior work from sources.bib. The concept folder must contain concept.json with a viability_score field.

items.description: Implement NumPy-vectorized O(N^2) force computation eliminating Python loops
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/gravity/vectorized.py using NumPy broadcasting to compute all pairwise forces without Python-level for-loops. Signature: compute_accelerations(positions, masses, softening) -> accelerations. Create tests/test_vectorized.py verifying: (a) output matches direct.py to within 1e-12 relative error for 100 random particles, (b) achieves at least 10x wall-clock speedup over direct.py for N=1000. Append vectorized benchmark results for N in {100, 500, 1000, 2000} to results/baseline_benchmarks.json.

items.description: Implement Barnes-Hut quadtree O(N log N) gravity solver
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/gravity/barnes_hut.py implementing: (a) QuadTree class with recursive 2D spatial decomposition and center-of-mass aggregation at internal nodes, (b) insert(position, mass) method, (c) compute_force(position, mass, theta=0.5) method using the opening-angle criterion, (d) compute_accelerations(positions, masses, softening, theta) top-level function matching the solver interface. Create tests/test_barnes_hut.py verifying: (i) force accuracy within 2% RMS of direct summation for 500 random particles with theta=0.5, (ii) all inserted particles are present (tree.count == N), (iii) theta=0 reduces to exact direct summation within 1e-10. All tests pass via pytest.

items.description: Implement adaptive timestep control using the Aarseth criterion
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/integrators/adaptive.py implementing timestep adaptation where dt_new = eta * sqrt(softening / max(|acceleration|)) with safety factor eta (default 0.01). Support global adaptive timestep mode (single dt for all particles). Create tests/test_adaptive.py verifying: (a) at least 1.5x speedup over fixed-timestep leapfrog for a collapsing cluster scenario (N=50, initially at rest), (b) energy conservation within 0.5% over the collapse, (c) timestep decreases during close encounters (dt_min < 0.1 * dt_initial). All tests pass via pytest.

items.description: Concept-tree evolution exploring optimization strategies beyond Barnes-Hut
items.acceptance_criteria: Use concept_evolve 'evolve' command on topic 'optimization strategies for N-body gravity beyond Barnes-Hut tree codes'. Verify results/concept_evolve/tree/ is updated with at least 3 new concept folders evaluating: particle-mesh (PM/P3M), fast multipole method (FMM-lite), spatial hashing, or learned force approximation. Each folder must contain concept.json with a viability_score (0-10) field. Produce results/concept_evolve/tree/optimizations/ranking.md ranking all candidates by feasibility for a minimal Python sim, referencing sources.bib for justification.

items.description: Implement the top-ranked novel optimization from concept-tree exploration
items.acceptance_criteria: Based on item_015 rankings, implement the highest-scored feasible optimization in src/gravity/<method_name>.py. Must include: (a) working implementation with compute_accelerations matching the solver interface, (b) at least 2 correctness tests in tests/test_<method_name>.py passing via pytest, (c) benchmark showing measurable speedup or accuracy improvement over vectorized.py for N >= 1000 (results appended to results/baseline_benchmarks.json). If no novel method is viable, document the negative result in results/concept_evolve/tree/optimizations/negative_result.md with specific technical reasons.

items.description: Delegate cross-domain reframing of gravity simulation via concept-tree-explorer subagent
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a concept-tree-explorer subagent using concept_evolve 'reframe' on 'efficient many-body gravitational force computation'. Produce results/concept_evolve/tree/cross_domain/reframings.md documenting at least 4 domain reframings (from: molecular dynamics, electrostatics, fluid SPH, game-engine physics, graph neural network force fields) with: (a) the key transferable insight from each domain, (b) at least 2 concrete actionable techniques that could improve the gravity sim, (c) references to papers from sources.bib where available. Add any newly discovered papers to sources.bib.

items.description: Run comprehensive scaling experiments across all implemented solvers
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute benchmarks for N in {10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000} across all implemented solvers (direct, vectorized, Barnes-Hut, and any novel Phase 3 solver) using leapfrog integration. For each (solver, N) pair, record: wall_time_seconds, energy_error_pct, angular_momentum_error_pct. Save to results/scaling_experiments.json. Produce figures/scaling_comparison.png as a log-log plot of wall-time vs N with fitted complexity curves labeled with big-O notation. The figure must contain at least 3 solver curves and be a valid PNG > 2KB.

items.description: Run integrator accuracy comparison on canonical test problems
items.acceptance_criteria: Compare Euler, fixed-step leapfrog, and adaptive leapfrog on: (a) two-body Kepler orbit with eccentricity 0.5 for 50 orbits, (b) Pythagorean three-body problem (masses 3, 4, 5 at right-triangle vertices) for 30 time units, (c) random 50-particle Plummer sphere for 50 dynamical times. Record: relative energy drift, wall-clock time per scenario. Save to results/integrator_comparison.json. Produce figures/energy_conservation.png (energy drift vs time for all integrators on test (a)) and figures/three_body_trajectories.png (Pythagorean problem paths). Both must be valid images > 1KB.

items.description: Conduct Barnes-Hut opening-angle (theta) sensitivity analysis
items.acceptance_criteria: For N=1000 random Plummer-distributed particles, sweep theta in {0.0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5}. Measure: RMS force error vs direct summation, wall-clock time per step, cumulative energy error after 100 steps. Save to results/theta_sensitivity.json. Produce figures/theta_sensitivity.png with dual y-axis (force error % on left, speedup factor on right, theta on x-axis). Identify and annotate the Pareto-optimal theta value achieving < 2% force error with maximum speedup.

items.description: Reproduce a published N-body benchmark and compare quantitatively against literature
items.acceptance_criteria: Select one benchmark from sources.bib (e.g., Plummer sphere cold collapse from Aarseth 2003, or a Kepler orbit regression test). Implement the exact initial conditions as described in the source. Run with at least 2 solvers. Produce: (a) figures/benchmark_reproduction.png showing qualitative trajectory comparison, (b) results/benchmark_reproduction.md with at least 2 quantitative metrics (e.g., half-mass radius evolution, energy conservation) compared against published values with percent error. Document must include explicit citations and state whether results are consistent with the reference within stated tolerances.

items.description: Delegate experiment synthesis: cross-reference results against literature claims via subagent
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a literature-graph-miner subagent to cross-reference experimental results from items 018-021 against performance claims in papers from sources.bib. Produce results/literature_comparison.md containing: (a) a comparison table with at least 5 rows comparing one metric from this project against a published value (columns: metric, our value, published value, paper citation, percent difference), (b) assessment of where the minimal sim matches, exceeds, or falls short with explanations, (c) at least 2 specific improvement recommendations based on techniques from the literature.

items.description: Write comprehensive technical report synthesizing all research findings
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/technical_report.md containing: (a) Abstract (150-300 words), (b) Introduction with problem motivation and contributions, (c) Related Work section citing at least 8 entries from sources.bib with comparative discussion, (d) Methods section describing all solver and integrator implementations with stated complexity, (e) Results section referencing at least 4 figures from figures/, (f) Discussion comparing performance against prior work from sources.bib, (g) Conclusion with limitations and 3 future work directions. Total length at least 3000 words.

items.description: Generate final concept-tree summary and research exploration map
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/concept_evolve/tree/final_summary.md synthesizing all concept-tree explorations from Phases 1-4. Must include: (a) ASCII tree visualization showing all concept branches and leaf nodes, (b) table of pursued vs pruned branches with one-sentence justification for each decision, (c) top 5 key insights from concept evolution with cross-references to where each insight was applied in the codebase, (d) at least 3 suggested future exploration branches with expected-value assessment (high/medium/low).

items.description: Update README.md with project overview, installation, usage, and results summary
items.acceptance_criteria: README.md contains: (a) title 'Minimal N-Body Gravity Simulation' and one-paragraph description, (b) installation instructions (Python version, pip install -r requirements.txt), (c) usage examples with sample commands for running each solver, (d) summary table of key results (solver, max N at real-time, energy error) with links to figures/, (e) repository structure diagram showing src/, tests/, results/, figures/ layout, (f) references section pointing to sources.bib. At least 400 words.

items.description: Create reproducibility package with pinned dependencies and automated pipeline script
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce: (a) requirements.txt with pinned versions (numpy, matplotlib, pytest at minimum), (b) run_all.py script that runs: all pytest tests, all benchmark sweeps, generates all figures, and prints a summary. 'python run_all.py' must complete without errors and produce all JSON files in results/ and all PNG files in figures/. (c) results/reproducibility_checklist.md listing every expected artifact file path with a generated/verified status.

items.description: Delegate final repository audit to concept-tree-explorer subagent for completeness verification
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch a concept-tree-explorer subagent to audit the entire repository. Produce results/final_audit.md with a pass/fail checklist verifying: (a) all 26 prior rubric items have corresponding output artifacts (list each item_id and its artifact path with pass/fail), (b) sources.bib has >= 10 entries and all are referenced in the technical report, (c) all figures referenced in the report exist in figures/ as valid images > 1KB, (d) concept tree at results/concept_evolve/tree/ has >= 3 branches with >= 2 leaves each, (e) all tests pass via 'pytest tests/', (f) run_all.py completes without errors. At least 22 of 26 prior items must pass for the audit to be considered successful.
